understanding: The attached LogCache implementation supports separate caller-owned lookup and write behaviors. Lookup captures a pointer under the cache read lock, then validates and copies it after unlocking; a miss delegates without filling the cache. Writing completes the backend call successfully before acquiring the cache lock and publishing input pointers. These separate operations expose interleaving boundaries without establishing that concurrent write/delete histories are permitted.

implementation_guards: Read the indexed cache slot under the cache read lock.
Accept a captured pointer only when it is non-nil and cached.Index equals idx.
reads: Cache length and slot at idx modulo cache length
Captured Log pointer and its Index after releasing the cache lock
writes: On a hit, shallow-copy the captured Log into the caller's output.
external_effects: Return nil after a cache-hit copy.
On a miss, invoke the backend GetLog with the original index and output pointer and return its result unchanged.
important_branches: A nil slot or mismatching index delegates to the backend.
Backend lookup success does not populate the cache.
Replacing the cache slice in DeleteRange does not revoke a pointer already captured by this lookup; the lookup does not recheck the slice before copying.
async_boundaries: Pointer capture ends at RUnlock; index validation and output copying occur outside the cache lock.
A miss invokes the backend after releasing the cache lock.
existing_protections: Cache slot access uses the same mutex as cache publication and invalidation.
The index comparison rejects a different index occupying the same ring slot.
unknowns: Caller serialization and permitted concurrent lookup, write, and deletion histories are not established.
Ownership and mutation restrictions for stored Log pointers and their referenced fields are unresolved.
A cache hit does not independently establish current backend presence or crash durability.

behaviors.execution_owner: Caller synchronously executing LogCache.StoreLogs, directly or through StoreLog.
behaviors.protocol_context: One input batch and LogCache wrapping a selected backend.
behaviors.trigger: StoreLogs(logs), or StoreLog(log) delegating a single-element batch.
implementation_guards: Return on a non-nil backend StoreLogs result before publishing any cache pointers for this invocation.
Hold the exclusive cache lock throughout the cache insertion loop.
reads: Input Log pointers and their indexes
writes: After backend success, assign each input pointer to cache[l.Index modulo cache length] in batch order.
durable_effects: Invoke the selected backend StoreLogs before acquiring the cache lock; persistence and partial-failure semantics depend on that backend.
external_effects: Return a formatted error on backend failure.
Return nil after backend success and completion of the cache insertion critical section.
important_branches: Backend failure prevents this invocation's cache insertion loop but does not establish absence of partial backend writes.
Entries colliding in a ring slot overwrite earlier assignments in batch order.
The cache stores input pointers without copying their Log values.
An empty successful batch performs no slot assignments.
async_boundaries: The backend call executes without holding the cache lock.
Backend success and cache publication are separate operations; DeleteRange can acquire the cache lock between them if callers permit concurrency.
The insertion loop has no deletion-generation check before publishing pointers.
existing_protections: Backend success is required before cache publication.
Cache slot publication is serialized with slice replacement and lookup slot capture by the shared mutex.
unknowns: Whether overlapping writes and deletions are legal for actual callers remains unresolved.
The selected backend and its ordering, partial-failure, and durability guarantees are unknown.
Successful cache publication does not establish continued slot occupancy or backend presence after concurrent operations.
